haiku-low.q1: Up to 10,000 rows: the CSV returns directly in the response. Above that (409), the page starts a background export; the user gets a status line, then an emailed 24-hour link.
haiku-low.q2: The active export is returned with 200 and no second job starts. Stale active rows, queued without a job_id over 5 minutes or untouched over 2 hours, are marked failed first.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The existing 7-day lifecycle rule on the exports bucket removes the stored file; expires_at is completion plus 7 days minus 1 hour.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, queued 60 s and 300 s apart. After the last failure, the export is marked failed, the page shows Failed with Try again, and a failure email is sent.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read replica. The export state row lives in the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row in the primary database. The page polls the latest-export endpoint every 5 seconds while queued or running, so reopening shows the same state.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica and writes 8 MB parts to a multipart upload. Only one page and one buffer are in memory, never the whole report.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing is visible, since the upload is aborted and parts discarded. The next attempt restarts from the first page, aborting the saved upload_id and starting a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: Filters and columns are stored on the export row, which holds up to 4 KB of filters. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job reads them from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. A conflicting insert returns the existing active row with 200 instead of a second job.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be completed and the row marked done first. On a rerun, if done with email_sent_at set, the job exits; if done without it, the job only sends the email.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED beyond this: the body is built fully in memory before sending, so no partial file is sent and nothing needs cleanup. Database errors return 500.

sonnet.q1: The page first calls the sync endpoint. If reports.row_count (replica) is 10,000 or fewer, the CSV is returned directly in the 200 response and nothing is stored. If above 10,000 (or the reader produces more than 10,000 rows), it returns 409 and the page calls the large-export endpoint in the same click. That creates an export row, queues a job (202), and the job streams rows into a multipart upload in the exports bucket, marks done, and emails a 24-hour link. The page also shows status and a Download button.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) for status queued/running allows only one active export. Stale active rows are first marked failed. If the insert conflicts, the existing active row is read and returned with 200, and no second job starts. The page shows that active export, even if its filters or cols differ from the URL.
sonnet.q3: The emailed link is a signed URL valid 24 hours (86400 s). The stored file is removed by an existing 7-day lifecycle rule on the exports bucket (not set up by this plan). The page offers downloads until expires_at (completed_at + 7 days - 1 hour), via fresh signed links.
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts (queue waits 60 s before attempt 2, 300 s before attempt 3). After attempt 3 fails, step 9 aborts any open upload, sets the row to failed with a short error_summary (max 500 chars, no row content), and sends a report_export_failed email only if it changed a row. The page shows 'Failed' with a Try again button.
sonnet.q5: The read replica (a read-only copy). Report rows and reports.row_count are read only from it.
sonnet.q6: Status is stored in the report_exports row (export row) in the primary database. The page polls GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, stopping on done/failed. On reopening or in a new tab, the page loads and calls latest, which returns the caller's most recent export (200) or 204 if none, with no id needed in the URL.
sonnet.q7: It streams: the keyset reader fetches 5,000-row pages (one in memory at a time), appends CSV bytes to an 8 MB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part. The whole report is never held in memory. Memory is one page plus one 8 MB buffer; a 900 MB CSV is about 115 parts. Load gate peak memory is 256 MB or less.
sonnet.q8: Data already written is in an open multipart upload; nothing is visible at the key until complete_multipart succeeds. On an exception, the attempt aborts the upload best-effort and sets the row to queued (if attempt < 3). If killed or the worker died, the upload stays open and the next attempt aborts it by the saved upload_id (or step 9 does after attempt 3). The next attempt starts from the first page with a new upload; earlier etags are never reused.
sonnet.q9: They are stored on the export row (filters text max 4 KB, and cols) in report_exports, captured from the click's request. The job payload contains only {export_id}; the job reads the row and passes its filters and cols to the shared reader.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status IN ('queued','running'). The losing insert conflicts, reads the existing active row, and returns it with 200, starting no second job.
sonnet.q11: The file must be complete (complete_multipart succeeded) and the row conditionally updated to status = done (with object_key, expires_at etc.); step 8 then runs, sending the email with a signed URL and setting email_sent_at. If the queue reruns the job: no row, failed, or done with email_sent_at set exits successfully; done with email_sent_at null goes to the email step only (new link, fresh 24 hours). Otherwise a running copy with equal or higher attempt exits.
sonnet.q12: Nothing is sent until the body is fully built, so no partial file exists and nothing needs cleaning up. The response is an error: 500 for a database error (400/403/404/409 for the other causes). The page shows that error's message and no export is started.
